title: Rembrandt's birth chart
metaDescription: Rembrandt's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 22.5° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a opposition: Mercury and Saturn within 0.4°, thinking wired to structure. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 22.5° Cancer: the third decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Jupiter. A water sign, read here in its third face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 2.4° Cancer, Venus holds 7.0° Gemini, Mars holds 26.9° Scorpio — in the old shorthand, a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste led by wit and proportion; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mercury directly across the wheel from Saturn, 0.4° off exact. The scheme reads an opposition as a axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit. Behind it, Mercury trine Jupiter at 0.7°, and Jupiter sextile Saturn at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Neptune while both square Venus. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Scorpio at 22.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Scorpio at 26.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Pisces at 1.7° is in domicile; Saturn in Capricorn at 2.8° is in domicile. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 5, earth 4, air 1 across the elements, and fixed 4, cardinal 3, mutable 3 across the modalities. Water signs hold memory in the scheme, where nothing is quite finished and little is genuinely forgotten. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.4° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 22.5°.
